title: A gentle request without required admission

captions.physics: Repeating requests for a required confirmation
captions.emotions: Feeling proportion in a mutual answer

meaning: You can speak bravely and gently while noticing when repeated asking requires a particular confirmation instead of a genuine proportionate answer.
text: The Devil in the physical position of your Vishuddha can appear in repeating a request until the required confirmation arrives. Strength in energy supports a wish to speak bravely and gently rather than hide what matters or obtain it through pressure. Justice in emotions brings proportion to mutual response. You can directly name discomfort without requiring admission of more than was said. A calm tone cannot make an answer free when only one formulation is permitted.

For example, after an awkward remark you ask “Admit you wanted to hurt me” although intention is unknown. You can gently name the words and your response without making a guess compulsory admission. **An honest answer need not confirm an attributed motive**. You ask about meaning and hear an actual explanation. Fairness appears when an unpleasant effect is recognised without demanding an answer for unestablished intention. Conversation gains a specific subject instead of testing one required version.

Pressure returns if precision refuses to hear experience altogether. An unconfirmed motive is then taken as proof that nothing unpleasant happened. Constructive Strength helps preserve consideration towards both sides. You can reject an attributed intention and directly answer for words spoken; proportion requires neither false admission nor cold cancellation of feeling merely because its cause remains under discussion between you.
